items.desc: Aerial footage shows the capsized Maltese-flagged Med Emre chemical tanker off the Spanish island of Ibiza.

items.title: Two dead after Iranian drone attack on Kuwait
items.desc: Kuwait’s army says two Italian workers were killed and four others were injured in an Iranian drone attack.

items.title: Pep Guardiola calls on world to ‘disobey horror’ over Gaza and praises BDS
items.desc: Football icon says it is more urgent than ever to demand an end to Israel's 'apartheid, colonialism and occupation'.

items.title: Iranian monarchists disrupt Paris event, highlighting bitter diaspora divide
items.desc: A Paris event on Iranian women's rights attended by French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot was disrupted when diaspora supporters of Reza Pahlavi, the US-based son of Iran's deposed shah, taunted left-leaning opponents of Iran's Islamic regime. The chaos underscored the bitter divides in the Iranian diaspora as the Iran war enters its tenth month.

items.title: Sanchez's big gamble: Will Spain swing from Socialists to hard right?
items.desc: For eight years, he’s been a mainstay among European leaders, one who’s snatched victory from the jaws of defeat before but has Pedro Sanchez run out of road this time? Spain's Socialist prime minister dogged by incumbent fatigue and nepotism allegations. Sanchez gambled on turning the rift in his coalition over his country's housing shortage into a referendum on his country's strong growth and calling a snap general election.

items.title: Hamas weighs response after Israel kills 10 people in Gaza
items.desc: Five Israeli strikes and a shooting overnight and on Thursday killed 10 Palestinians across Gaza, according to officials at Shifa and Al-Aqsa Martyrs hospitals, where the casualties were taken. A strike on a residential apartment in Deir Al-Balah in central Gaza killed a man and his wife, the officials said. FRANCE 24's Jennie Shin speaks with journalist Ahmed Dremly, who was in Gaza until six months ago and has extensively covered the humanitarian crisis there.

items.title: Trump urges Putin to end 'military aggression' in Europe
items.desc: US President Donald Trump said Thursday he had asked Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression" against Europe, in a shift in tone towards the leader Russian he called his friend just a week ago. Trump said he had made the request to Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine. The US leader's comments come a day after he hosted NATO chief Mark Rutte in Florida, after which they issued a joint statement calling on Russia not to expand the Ukraine war. FRANCE 24's international affairs editor Kethevane Gorjestani explains.

items.title: France's Bardella faces new allegations of anti
items.desc: French far-right leader Jordan Bardella on Thursday faced new accusations of having made anti-Semitic remarks as a teenager, after French media published extracts from previously unaired conversations online. The 31-year-old top ally of French presidential candidate Marine Le Pen has denied any wrongdoing after allegations emerged in September that he made conspiracist comments about Jewish people on Facebook in 2013. FRANCE 24's Solange Mougin reports.

items.title: Le Pen slams push for EU budget deal before French election
items.desc: EU leaders locked horns over the bloc's budget at a summit meeting in Brussels on Thursday, as far-right leader Marine Le Pen slammed an "underhanded" push to lock in the long-term spending plans before French presidential elections next year. European Council head Antonio Costa turned up the pressure upon arrival at the budget talks, where heavyweight Germany is pressing for cuts as well as burden-sharing on money for Ukraine. FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels.

items.title: French far-right leader Jordan Bardella faces fresh allegations of anti
items.desc:
The leader of France's far-right National Rally party, Jordan #Bardella, is facing fresh accusations of having made anti-Semitic remarks as a teenager. 
 
On Thursday, November 26, French media outlets Mediapart and Le Monde published new excerpts from private Facebook conversations dating back to 2013.

items.title: Reporters Without Borders demands suspension of controversial French TV channel CNews
items.desc: Paris-based international press freedom group Reporters Without Borders (RSF) on Thursday called on France's media regulator Arcom to suspend right-wing channel CNews for one month over its failure to uphold pluralism. The news channel owned by conservative billionaire Vincent Bolloré condemned the call for its suspension.

items.title: Will Spain's far right replace Europe's left
items.desc: Some 39 million Spaniards will head to the ballot this Sunday to vote in early general elections. Latest polls put the conservative Popular Party ahead of incumbent PM Pedro Sanchez’s Socialists. The third-strongest political force, however, is the far-right Vox party. A strong showing at Sunday’s election could see them form Spain’s next government. FRANCE 24 explains.

items.title: ACROSS AFRICA:  Tunisian Photographer's Family Focus
items.desc: Stories from the continent with Georja Calvin-Smith. This week, health workers struggling to keep pace with DR Congo's Ebola outbreak say they feel abandoned and unsupported. Also, the World Cup was about more than winning... for some fans, at least. Tunisia's performance may not have been all that its supporters had hoped, but sports photographer Hosni Manoubi is far from negative about a family tradition of documenting his country's international sports showings. [Archive Episode, June 2026]

items.title: In California, exceptional tides and nearly 9m-high waves batter the coast
items.desc: USA: Powerful waves and king tides destroyed part of a pier in Pacifica, south of San Francisco, on Wednesday. In Marin County, authorities issued a temporary evacuation order and urged people to stay away from the beach.

items.title: Spanish economist de Cos to succeed Lagarde as head of ECB
items.desc: Spanish monetary economist Pablo Hernandez de Cos on Thursday was set to replace France's Christine Lagarde as the new head of the European Central Bank (ECB). His nomination comes as the Europe's most powerful financial institution grapples with an Iran war-driven resurgence in inflation and a cost of living crisis.

items.title: Lost homes, stolen freedom: National Book Award winners on exile and imprisonment
items.desc: Two books about losing everything have just won America's most prestigious literary honours. Hannah Lillith Assadi took the National Book Award for fiction for "Paradiso 17", a novel inspired by her late father, who was driven from Palestine in 1948 during the Nakba. Abdelrahman ElGendy won the non-fiction prize for "Huna", his memoir of six years as a political prisoner in Egypt, arrested at 17 alongside his father. ElGendy couldn't be in New York to collect his award: his visa was denied.

items.title: How far-right Vox is winning over young voters ahead of Spain's snap election
items.desc: Spain's Vox party is winning over many young people ahead of the country's snap election on November 29, particularly men. The far-right party is capitalising on the rising cost of living and anti-immigrant sentiment to expand its once-marginal electoral base.

items.title: Across Africa: The Scars of South Africa's Soweto Uprising
items.desc: 50 years ago, thousands of young South Africans from Soweto protested against apartheid's stranglehold on their education  and the imposition of Afrikaans as a language of instruction. What began as a peaceful protest ended in bloodshed. And men in Northern Benin confront uncomfortable realities about the lives of the women who live and love them.  [Archive edition, June 2026]

items.title: From leadership crises to tech outages, can corporations rebuild public trust?
items.desc: From cyberattacks to network failures to leadership crises, tech corporations are showing signs of vulnerability. The dramatic resignation and return of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has underscored the potential risk of depending on a single leader, both for the company and the entire AI industry. Meanwhile, global outages at Microsoft and a number of US banks have showcased declining public trust in institutions.

items.title: French woman on trial for IS group propaganda tells court she’s ‘ashamed’
items.desc: The trial of Émilie König, one of France's most high-profile Islamic State (IS) group recruits, opened in a Paris court on Thursday with the 41-year-old mother of five apologising to her children, mother and the "French nation" for her actions. König travelled in 2012 to Syria, where she appeared in the jihadist group's propaganda videos. She was repatriated to France in 2022.

items.title: Season's eatings! Celebrating Thanksgiving in France
items.desc: This Thursday marks Thanksgiving in the United States, the biggest travel holiday of the year there and arguably the most important on US calendars. But here in France, it's just another day. However, Americans living in Paris do try to capture the Thanksgiving spirit, though it can be tricky to track down the turkeys and pies required. Joining us to discuss how Americans do Thanksgiving in Paris is Cordon Bleu-trained chef and the owner of Boneshaker Donuts, Amanda Bankert.

items.title: Madagascar's near-total abortion ban puts women's lives at risk
items.desc: November 25 marked the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. Activists argue that tackling gender-based violence also means addressing the wider inequalities that put women at risk, including restrictions on reproductive rights. In Madagascar, abortion is almost entirely banned, even in cases of rape, incest or when a woman's life is at risk. FRANCE 24’s Aurélie Kouman reports on the consequences of the country's strict laws, which force thousands of women to seek unsafe, clandestine procedures.

items.title: Fighting in eastern Congo forces Ebola workers to evacuate, disrupts outbreak response
items.desc: Escalating fighting in eastern Congo has forced Ebola response workers to leave affected areas and disrupted efforts to contain the deadliest outbreak in the country, health officials and humanitarian workers said Wednesday. Congo’s Ebola outbreak has infected more than 11,700 people and killed more than 5,700 since it was declared in May, according to the latest government data. FRANCE 24's Emmet Livingstone reports from Kinshasa, DR Congo.

items.title: Moscow drone incursions: Poland to create no-fly zone at Ukraine border
items.desc: Poland will soon create a no-fly zone near the Ukrainian border, a deputy defence minister announced on Wednesday, after several incursions into its airspace it blamed on Russia. Poland backs Ukraine as it fights off Russia's near five-year invasion and has repeatedly accused Moscow of seeking to target Kyiv's supporters with drone incursions and other methods.

items.title: Émilie König, 'the muse of the Islamic State group' goes on trial in France
items.desc: French anti-terrorism prosecutors once dubbed her "the muse of the Islamic State group". On Thursday, Émilie König appears before a special criminal court in Paris, seeking to convince judges that she has been deradicalised. Originally from western France, König spent a decade in Syria and is accused of being one of the Islamic State group's most active French propagandists. Charged with criminal association with a terrorist organisation, she maintains that she has no blood on her hands.
